bull_case_summary: IOI Properties improved CFO alongside an expanded revenue base. Round two correctly separates this cash observation from fair-value and remeasurement gains, preserving a conditional operating-expansion thesis that still requires funded returns on acquired assets.
bear_case_summary: Large noncash profit additions, lower Q4 earnings and higher borrowings qualify apparent headline cheapness. Round two accepts that some improvement is cash-backed but notes CFO excludes acquisition investment and does not establish recurring distributable cash or deleveraging.
key_points_of_agreement: CFO improvement is real and distinct from noncash gains.
Reported EPS cannot directly represent recurring earning power.
Borrowings growth and investment outlays require a matched cash bridge.
Oversold RSI does not establish a bottom.
key_points_of_disagreement: Whether the cash-backed operating anchor meaningfully advances a prospective investment thesis before post-investment returns are verified.
unresolved_uncertainties: Recurring earnings excluding fair-value and remeasurement effects.
Acquisition and maintenance investment, debt service and distributable cash.
Adequate returns on the enlarged debt-funded asset base.
Matched valuation rather than the vendor headline P/E.
